title: Management Accounting Practices and Organisational Performance Management in Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises in Soweto: A Systematic Review
content: Introduction: Management accounting practices, including costing, budgeting, performance measurement, decision support and accounting information systems, are frequently linked with improved SME performance. However, the supplied evidence also indicates that benefits depend on organisational capability, information quality, management commitment, participation and implementation conditions. Direct evidence from SMEs located specifically in Soweto is absent from the supplied synthesis. Methods: The researcher-selected databases and information sources were Google Scholar and ERIC. The eligibility protocol restricted publication years to from 2020. The exact calendar date of search execution was not recorded in the verified identification provenance; this is distinct from the publication-year eligibility range. Google Scholar and ERIC were the researcher-selected information sources. The eligibility period was from 2020, while the search execution date was not recorded. Results: Costing, budgeting and performance evaluation were recurring practices. The dominant evidence pattern associated management accounting with improved financial, operational and managerial performance, although direct effects were inconsistent and mediated pathways were common. Budgeting, intellectual capital, performance measurement, decision quality and reporting quality acted as important mechanisms. Resource constraints, limited expertise, weak formalisation, inadequate information, cybersecurity concerns and limited risk-management capability restricted effective implementation. Participative, ethical and risk-aware use strengthened organisational relevance. Discussion/Conclusion: Management accounting practices appear generally beneficial when embedded in capable organisational systems rather than adopted as isolated tools. Nevertheless, conclusions for Soweto remain cautious because no supplied study directly examined Soweto SMEs. Future research should generate location-specific, longitudinal and methodologically transparent evidence focused on township, informal, micro and small-enterprise conditions.
